PullRequest.Title: sessions: improve filtered Remote picker results
PullRequest.Body:
Addresses follow-up feedback from #335890.

- show matching Remote entries directly in the unified new-session picker while filtering instead of keeping them behind `Remote >`
- make nested action-list filters own their keyboard and dismissal behavior without blocking unrelated workbench shortcuts
- complete nested submenu hover, footer, scrolling, pointer-intent, and constrained-layout behavior
- add regression coverage for the Remote picker and shared action list

Validation:
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts` (210 passing)
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `git diff --check`

Fixes #336181

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The listener registration change, non-persistent Remote submenu options, synchronous ListView render-before-notification ordering, and geometry-heavy callback are all directly traced. Exact frame loss varies by device, menu complexity, and scroll input rate, which affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous DOM geometry/style work on the UI thread
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One complete panel-positioning pass is now executed for every emitted wheel, trackpad, touch, smooth-scroll, or programmatic scroll update while a child panel is open; cost therefore scales with scroll-event frequency.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated style/layout work on the scroll critical path can increase scroll latency and drop frames.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The scroll listener was registered only for widgets with persistentHover. Nested Remote submenu widgets are non-persistent, so scrolling them did not invoke their open child hover's layout callback.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every ActionListWidget now subscribes to onDidScroll and synchronously invokes _layoutSubmenu whenever any child panel is open.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 1054-1058 replace the prior `if (this._options?.persistentHover)` registration guard with an unconditional onDidScroll subscription that calls `_layoutSubmenu` for non-persistent nested lists.
Findings.Title: Coalesce submenu relayouts during scrolling
Findings.Impact: With a status hover open in a long Remote submenu, wheel or trackpad scrolling now performs panel geometry reads and style writes on every scroll update, putting extra layout work directly on the interaction path and risking visible jank.
Findings.Evidence: ListView registers its internal scroll listener first and `onScroll` calls `render(...)`, which mutates/recycles rows; this new listener then calls `_layoutSubmenu`. That callback reads the list, anchor, and panel via multiple `getBoundingClientRect()`/`offsetHeight` accesses and writes panel position (and, for constrained nested menus, relayouts the submenu list). The added regression test explicitly observes one `_layoutSubmenu` call for one nested-list scroll, and the Remote test uses a non-persistent filtered submenu, proving the changed path is reachable.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep immediate relayout for explicit layout/filter operations, but coalesce scroll-triggered submenu positioning to at most once per animation frame and cancel any pending callback when the submenu is cleared or the widget is disposed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and type in the consolidated new-session workspace picker so Remote submenu entries appear as direct filtered results.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening synchronously rebuilds items from already-loaded recents, providers, browse actions, and menu actions before rendering. Each input event synchronously scans top-level items plus the Remote item's filterItems and splices the matching rows; no external operation blocks filtering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: T top-level rows plus R effective Remote rows (deduplicated recents plus registered providers/browse/menu actions). A child-only query checks R children; a parent-label match renders all R children.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded synchronous item construction/filtering and list rendering; no asynchronous filter delegate or parallel boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Providers, recents, and menu actions are already in memory. filterItems are rebuilt per picker construction and filtering has no result cache; cold and warm opens therefore have the same O(T+R) local work, without new cache misses or remote fetches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added filterItems arrays and _applyFilter loop are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users with unusually large remote histories pay more allocation/rendering, but normal effective cardinality is expected to be modest and no boundary work is multiplied.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the added O(R) local objects and substring checks implement the requested direct results and do not establish a concrete user-visible regression at realistic cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select or remove a Remote result exposed directly by the unified filter.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selection dismisses the picker and then may await one provider browse/connect operation or one workspace validation; removal invokes one recent-workspace update or one host disconnect/removal. These operations are after the user commits one row, not on filtering or rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect an on-demand remote provider via provider.connect(), or run the selected provider browse action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one provider operation for the single selected result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Selecting the same entry through Remote > executed the same provider operation once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited after selection before the workspace can be accepted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check existence of a selected file-scheme workspace with fileService.exists().
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one check for the selected workspace, and only for file-scheme URIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same selected workspace was validated after selection through the submenu.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited after selection; absent from typing and submenu scrolling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Disconnect/remove one remote host or update its persisted configuration when the row's remove action is invoked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One host per explicit remove gesture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing submenu row exposed the same onRemove callback and operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs only after explicit removal, not before filtered results appear.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One committed result; no per-result fan-out occurs across the filtered collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One selected/remove action is dispatched; no new burst or parallel loop is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Connected providers avoid provider.connect(); disconnected on-demand providers perform one connect. The diff does not alter connection or validation caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct filter items carry the same folder/provider, browse action, run, and onRemove semantics as the pre-existing submenu actions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency varies, but cardinality and placement are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff changes discoverability, not boundary-operation count, concurrency, or critical-path placement after selection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, filter, and scroll a non-persistent nested action-list submenu while a child hover/submenu panel is visible, including the Remote host status list.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening constructs the nested widget and measures its rows locally; typing filters locally. During scrolling, ListView first renders/recycles rows and the newly unconditional listener then synchronously invokes the child panel's geometry/layout callback before the scroll event returns.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: R submenu rows control one-time construction/filtering; S emitted scroll updates control the regression, with one synchronous panel-positioning pass per update while a child panel remains open.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Scroll rendering and submenu geometry work are serialized synchronously on the UI thread. There is no requestAnimationFrame coalescing or backpressure for the added callback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache applies to DOM geometry. Every scroll notification re-reads live rectangles/offsets and rewrites panel styles.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: listener ordering, row rendering, geometry reads/style writes, non-persistent submenu options, and the added scroll-layout test are directly present in the repository.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame impact depends on device, scroll event rate, zoom, and whether the constrained-layout branches run; the synchronous per-event mechanism is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: the diff moves synchronous geometry/layout work onto every nested-list scroll update without coalescing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use nested action-list keyboard handling, footer sizing, and hover content in permission and agent-host pickers.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening allocates hover MarkdownString objects and performs one footer width/height measurement; nested-filter keydown performs one soft keybinding resolution. Permission/agent-host mappings clear inherited filterItems while mapping their existing rows.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: H hover-bearing child actions at submenu creation and one resolver lookup per nested-filter keydown; permission/agent-host mapping remains one property assignment per existing row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All work is synchronous and serialized; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is reached by these changed rendering/key-handling lines.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The keybinding resolver is the existing service resolver; hover objects live with the open submenu and are disposed with it. No changed long-lived cache or retained key set was found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: allocations, measurements, resolver call, and disposal ownership are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Menu sizes and typing rates vary, but each added operation is bounded and lightweight relative to the existing widget render/filter path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: these changes add bounded per-open/per-key work and no realistic standalone performance degradation was established.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. One medium-confidence-severity synchronous UI/layout regression was submitted for uncoalesced nested-submenu relayout on every scroll update; filtering, selection boundaries, object allocation, footer/hover rendering, and keybinding dispatch introduced no additional reportable regression.
